text: around the nose - complaining about a strange smell that no one else can detect. If you think your child may have something stuck in their nose take them to see a doctor. ## Non-urgent treatment for coughing and wheezing Generally, you can relieve mild coughing and wheezing at home. Usually, the coughing will clear up in a few days to a couple of weeks. If mild coughing goes on for three weeks, see your doctor. Home care suggestions for mild coughing and wheezing in children include: - comfort your child – try to keep your child calm. Having a cough and a noisy wheeze frightens children and breathing is more difficult when they are upset - offer frequent drinks – drinking smaller amounts, but more often, may be easier if they are blocked up from a cold - avoid smoking – smoking in the home or car increases the risk of respiratory problems in children. Medicines such as antibiotics don’t help viral infections such as colds, flu, bronchiolitis or

source_title: Coughing and wheezing in children | Better Health Channel
text: from a cold - avoid smoking – smoking in the home or car increases the risk of respiratory problems in children. Medicines such as antibiotics don’t help viral infections such as colds, flu, bronchiolitis or croup. ‘Over-the-counter’ cough medicines are not suitable for infants and young children without specific advice from your child’s doctor, as there is evidence that they may cause harm to some children and mask symptoms of more serious illness. ## Where to get help - In an emergency, call triple zero (000) - Emergency department of your nearest hospital - Virtual Emergency Department - Urgent Care Clinics - Nurse-on-call Tel. 1300 606 024 – for expert health information and advice (24 hours, 7 days) - Maternal and Child Health Line Tel. 13 22 29 (24 hours) - Asthma Australia Helpline Tel. 1800 278 462 - Your GP (doctor) - Your local community health centre ## Asthma , 2018, Royal Children’s Hospital. - Bronchiolitis (wheezing babies) , Child and Youth Health, South Australian Government. - Sung V

source_title: Breathing support and MND
text: Respiratory care record: Breathing support and MND Category: mnd_respiratory_guidance Publisher: MND Australia URL: https://www.mndaustralia.org.au/mnd-connect/living-with-mnd/breathing-and-mnd Description: MND-specific guidance about respiratory muscle weakness, symptoms, assessment, monitoring and support options. Care team notes: Ask the MND clinic, respiratory physician, physiotherapist and GP about baseline respiratory testing, warning signs, cough strength and when to seek urgent help.

source_title: Non-invasive ventilation in MND
text: Respiratory care record: Non-invasive ventilation in MND Category: niv_bipap Publisher: MND Australia URL: https://www.mndaustralia.org.au/mnd-connect/for-health-professionals-service-providers/managing-symptoms/breathing-management-in-mnd Description: MND respiratory and NIV guidance relevant to nocturnal hypoventilation, BiPAP/NIV setup, monitoring and ongoing review. Care team notes: Escalate morning headaches, daytime sleepiness, breathlessness lying flat, poor sleep, repeated chest infections, weak cough or mask/interface problems to respiratory clinicians.

source_title: Cough strength and airway clearance
text: Respiratory care record: Cough strength and airway clearance Category: cough_airway_clearance Publisher: MND Australia / Lung Foundation Australia URL: https://www.mndaustralia.org.au/mnd-connect/living-with-mnd/breathing-and-mnd Description: Guidance relevant to weak cough, secretions, mucus clearance, cough-assist discussions and chest infection risk. Care team notes: Discuss cough effectiveness, airway clearance techniques, secretion management, suction/cough-assist equipment and chest infection action plans with respiratory and allied health teams.

source_title: Breathlessness and urgent escalation
text: Respiratory care record: Breathlessness and urgent escalation Category: breathlessness_escalation Publisher: Healthdirect Australia URL: https://www.healthdirect.gov.au/shortness-of-breath Description: Australian general guidance on shortness of breath, red flags and when emergency care may be needed. Care team notes: Use emergency services for severe or sudden breathlessness, blue lips, chest pain, confusion, fainting or other urgent symptoms; use MND respiratory plans for known progressive symptoms.

source_title: Saliva and secretion management
text: Respiratory care record: Saliva and secretion management Category: saliva_secretions Publisher: MND Australia URL: https://www.mndaustralia.org.au/mnd-connect/for-health-professionals-service-providers/managing-symptoms/saliva-management-in-mnd Description: MND-specific saliva and secretion guidance that may affect breathing comfort, cough, airway clearance and choking/aspiration risk. Care team notes: Ask speech pathology, respiratory clinicians and medical teams about saliva thickness, drooling, suction, medication options, hydration, swallowing safety and secretion clearance.
